title: English File Upper-Intermediate, File 2: present perfect simple and continuous; adjectives (check against the book)

fixIt.text: I've knowing her since primary school.
fixIt.explain: know is a state verb: present perfect simple, I've known.

fixIt.text: I've been read this book for weeks and I still haven't finished it.
fixIt.explain: have been + -ing: an activity still going on.

fixIt.text: It's been raining since three hours.
We've painted the kitchen all morning.
fixIt.explain: all morning = an activity over time: have been painting.

fixIt.text: My grandmother has lived in this house for she was born.
fixIt.explain: since + a moment in the past.

fixIt.text: He's been working as a guide since ten years.
The government should do more for the poors.
fixIt.explain: the + adjective for a group of people has no -s: the poor, the rich.

fixIt.text: The elderlies in our village need better healthcare.

builder.text: We have known each other for years.

radio.title: Twenty years at the market
radio.text: Mrs Chanthy has been selling vegetables at the same market for twenty years. She has known most of her customers since they were children, and some of them now bring their own children. Prices have changed a lot, and she has been thinking about retiring, but she says the market keeps her young. The elderly in her street often sit at her stall and talk for hours. She has never taken a holiday.
